name: Claude Code
description: Terminal coding agent with an Anthropic-compatible gateway setting.
instructions: Merge env settings in ~/.claude/settings.json: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.cometapi.com, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=your CometAPI key, and ANTHROPIC_MODEL=an exact CometAPI Anthropic-compatible model ID.
Restart Claude Code and inspect /status. Remove a conflicting stored ANTHROPIC_API_KEY when using bearer-token authentication.
caveats: Use the API origin without /v1; this client uses the Anthropic Messages protocol.
Process environment, project settings or managed settings can override user settings.
First-run setup and workspace trust remain under the user's control.

name: Codex CLI
description: Coding agent supporting a custom Responses API provider.
instructions: In ~/.codex/config.toml, add a cometapi model provider with base_url=https://api.cometapi.com/v1 and wire_api=responses, then select model_provider=cometapi and a CometAPI Responses-compatible model.
Supply authentication through env_key=COMETAPI_API_KEY with a launcher, or the supported experimental_bearer_token field in the private user config. Restart the CLI.
caveats: Modern Codex only supports Responses, not Chat Completions.
A direct bearer token in config is plaintext; the official documentation prefers an environment-backed key.
An active profile may override the selected model. CLI configuration does not guarantee that every desktop or cloud task uses this provider.

name: Aider
description: Terminal pair programmer with a documented user YAML configuration.
instructions: Merge openai-api-base: https://api.cometapi.com/v1, openai-api-key: your key, and model: openai/<CometAPI model ID> into ~/.aider.conf.yml.
Restart Aider in your project.
caveats: The openai/ prefix selects Aider's routing provider; it is not part of the raw CometAPI model ID.
Project configuration, weak-model and editor-model settings may keep other models active.
Unknown models can require verified model metadata or an edit-format setting.
Some models need additional Aider metadata, such as use_temperature: false or an output allowance for reasoning. Endpoint and key setup does not configure every model capability.

name: Continue
description: VS Code, JetBrains and CLI assistant with local YAML model definitions.
instructions: Add a CometAPI model to ~/.continue/config.yaml using provider: openai, apiBase: https://api.cometapi.com/v1, apiKey: your key, and the exact model ID.
Select Local Config and the CometAPI model in Continue. Use roles chat, edit and apply; configure other roles only for models that support them.
caveats: Creating config.yaml supersedes legacy config.json; preserve or migrate existing settings first.
Cloud or saved configurations can remain selected until switched in the app.
Shell exports are insufficient for IDE extensions; separate secrets can use ~/.continue/.env.

name: OpenCode
description: Open-source coding agent with custom model-provider configuration.
instructions: Check the installed OpenCode major version and edit the global opencode.json or opencode.jsonc under ~/.config/opencode.

For v1 add provider.cometapi with npm=@ai-sdk/openai-compatible and options.baseURL=https://api.cometapi.com/v1 plus options.apiKey. For v2 use providers.cometapi, package=@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible and settings instead.
Declare the exact model in the provider and select model=cometapi/<model ID>.
caveats: Automatic setup is verified for OpenCode 1. OpenCode 2 is a separate beta executable (opencode2) with a changing schema; its setup is guided.
Use a Responses provider package for Responses-only models.
Project, custom-path and managed configurations can override the global model.

name: Gemini CLI
description: Google's coding CLI with a native Gemini API base override.
instructions: Automatic setup supports npm Gemini CLI 0.58.0 on macOS/Linux with bash or zsh, and 0.60.0 on Windows in the standard PowerShell 7 console. The helper installs a private launcher and shell function for new interactive terminals.
The helper writes native API-key authentication and a Gemini model in .gemini/settings.json. It provides GEMINI_API_KEY and GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL only to the launched CLI.
caveats: Gemini uses its native protocol at https://api.cometapi.com, without an OpenAI /v1 suffix.
Gemini CLI 0.23.0 is not supported for automatic setup because it does not honor the isolated home setting.

Existing shell aliases/functions and incompatible entry-point layouts require a dedicated adapter. Windows CMD, Windows PowerShell 5, custom-host profiles and shells that disable profile loading are not configured. Execution policy remains unchanged. Reopen the terminal after setup. Absolute-path invocations do not load the shell function.
Workspace trust, existing tools and approvals remain unchanged. An untrusted workspace may still need its normal explicit trust decision.

name: Goose
description: Open-source desktop and CLI agent with custom OpenAI-compatible providers.
instructions: Open Goose Settings or goose configure and create a custom OpenAI-compatible provider named CometAPI.
Use the full custom-provider URL https://api.cometapi.com/v1/chat/completions, enter the exact model ID, and enter the key through Goose's credential prompt.
Select the new provider and model, then start a new Goose session.
caveats: API keys in config.yaml are ignored; Goose uses the system keyring or its configured secret-storage backend.
Current config uses active_provider/providers; older flat GOOSE_PROVIDER and GOOSE_MODEL fields are legacy.
Custom provider URL semantics differ from a generic OpenAI base URL.

name: Zed
description: Code editor with custom OpenAI-compatible model access.
instructions: Run agent: open settings in Zed and choose Add Provider under LLM Providers.
Create an OpenAI-compatible CometAPI provider with API URL https://api.cometapi.com/v1, the exact model ID and its verified context limit.
Enter the key in Zed's provider UI and select that model.
caveats: API keys belong in Zed's credential UI or provider environment variable, not settings.json.
Responses-only models need capabilities.chat_completions=false.
External agents and terminal threads have their own provider configuration.

name: Cline
description: Coding assistant with an OpenAI Compatible provider selection.
instructions: Open Cline Settings and select OpenAI Compatible as the API provider.
Set Base URL to https://api.cometapi.com/v1, enter your CometAPI key, and enter the exact model ID.
Use Verify when available, and select compatible tool/image capabilities only if supported by the model.
caveats: The extension's credential store is not a supported external configuration file.
Model tool calling and streaming compatibility must match the selected model.

name: Roo Code
description: Coding extension with an OpenAI-compatible provider and native tools.
instructions: Open Roo Code Settings and select OpenAI Compatible.
Enter https://api.cometapi.com/v1, your CometAPI key and an exact model ID supporting native OpenAI-style tool calling.
caveats: Native tool calling is required; Roo no longer offers an XML tool fallback.
Use the extension's supported settings or import UI for credentials.

name: Kilo Code
description: Coding agent and extension with custom providers across several API protocols.
instructions: Open Kilo Settings → Providers and add a custom provider with ID cometapi.
For Chat Completions use OpenAI Compatible and base URL https://api.cometapi.com/v1; select Responses or Messages for models requiring those protocols.
Enter your CometAPI key, add the exact model ID and choose it from the model picker.
caveats: Current Kilo uses kilo.json(c) provider configuration; older extensions use different storage.
Global config can resolve environment/file secrets; repository config has tighter secret-resolution restrictions.
Context limits and native tool capabilities should match the model's verified metadata.

name: VS Code / GitHub Copilot Chat
description: VS Code chat and agent features can use a Custom Endpoint provider.
instructions: Run Chat: Manage Language Models in VS Code, choose Add Models → Custom Endpoint, and name the group CometAPI.
Enter the key through the secure input prompt and select the matching API type.

In chatLanguageModels.json, use vendor=customendpoint and configure the exact model plus its full endpoint: https://api.cometapi.com/v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses or /v1/messages as appropriate. Select the model in chat.
caveats: The old github.copilot.chat.customOAIModels setting is deprecated.
Keys should use secure input variables rather than a private database edit.
This configures chat/agent and utility tasks; inline completions and embedding-dependent features have separate requirements.
